== Biography ==
James Glasgow was a cooper.

James was born about 1800. He passed away about 1880.

== Research Notes ==
=== Pittsylvania records and unproved parents — 23 October 2026 ===

The inspected [https://www.usgenwebsites.org/vagenweb/pittsylvania/deaths/1860Deaths.htm USGenWeb 1860 Pittsylvania death transcription] records James Glasgow, cooper, age 71 years 10 months 12 days, Pittsylvania birthplace, cause '''“killed,”''' and Susan Glasgow as informant and wife. Its parent column and exact death-date cell are blank. This is a modern transcription of county returns; the original register was not inspected. The existing 28 September 1860 date comes from the previously cited death index, FHL 2048580. Combining that date with the transcribed age yields 16 November 1788; this is a calculated birthday, not independent birth evidence, so the approximate birth field is retained.

The [https://www.usgenwebsites.org/vagenweb/pittsylvania/marriages/1767marriage.pdf#page=104 marriage-bond compilation], printed p. 101/PDF p. 104, visually checked 23 October, gives James Glasgow/Susanna High, 21 October 1818, with Freeman High bondsman and no James parent. Printed p. 83/PDF p. 86 separately records Robert Eudaley/Elizabeth Glasgow, 22 December 1815, with Robert Glasgow bondsman and no parent annotation. That Robert is a local associated lead, not an established father or a proved brother/sister link. The compilation is not the original bond; inspect its consent/signatures next.

A [https://www.ancestry.com/genealogy/records/james-glasgow-24-1csrc5 contributed Ancestry aggregation] names Robert Glasgow 1760–1839 and Sarah Cooper 1763–1853 as parents, without an inspected supporting record. No named parent is selected from this claim. [[Glasgow-1530|Robert-1530]] has matching years but is a documented Glasgow weaver with Jack/Brash marriages; he is not identified by a year match. [[Glasgow-12|Robert-12]], the Ohio immigrant with different wives, remains unconnected to this household. [[Glasgow-395|Robert-395]] is specifically inconsistent: his son James was already dead in a 1837 newspaper account, whereas this cooper lived to 1860. [[Glasgow-357|William-357]] and his Sarah Cooper 1756–1812 are a different Currituck couple; neither can be renamed or imported to fill this gap. The 1815 bond may help identify a local family, but does not establish the contributed Robert/Sarah couple.
